blocks.title: Consequences of Non-Compliance exam shortcuts
items: Example: Organization pays $500,000 for a compliance violation.
Sanctions are broader official penalties or restrictions.
Example: Regulator limits what the company may offer.
Customers stop trusting the organization → REPUTATIONAL DAMAGE
This is a trust and credibility impact.
Example: Customers leave after a public compliance scandal.
Organization can no longer legally provide a service → LOSS OF LICENSE
Required authorization has been revoked or suspended.
Vendor agreement is terminated because compliance terms were violated → CONTRACTUAL IMPACT
The consequence comes from contract terms.
Example: Customer cancels the agreement and seeks damages.
blocks.example: Focus on whether the scenario is about proving compliance, maintaining compliance, consequences of failure, or privacy/data-handling responsibilities.

questions.q: A regulator imposes a $500,000 monetary penalty for a compliance violation. Which consequence is this?
questions.explanation: A fine is a direct monetary penalty.

questions.q: A government authority restricts a company's ability to offer a certain service. Which consequence is this?
questions.explanation: A sanction is an official restriction or penalty imposed by an authority.

questions.q: Customers stop trusting a company after a public compliance failure. Which consequence is this?
questions.explanation: Reputational damage affects trust, credibility, and public confidence.

questions.q: A professional organization can no longer legally provide a regulated service because its authorization was revoked. Which consequence is this?
questions.explanation: Loss of license means required permission to operate or provide a service has been revoked.

questions.q: A customer terminates a vendor contract because the vendor violated contractual compliance terms. Which consequence is this?
questions.explanation: Contractual impacts arise from violating obligations in an agreement.
